messages.author: 36372c17d23b31c8
messages.subject: How to plot log(Y / λ) ?
parts:
Hi,

I have been trying CODEX for CNV calling and I have got pretty good results so far. For visual validation, I would like to generate log(Y / λ) plots like you have done in the manuscript for ATRX gene. Is there a function in CODEX for this purpose? Can you please help?

Thank you,
Bekir

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] How to plot log(Y / λ) ?
parts:
Hi Bekir,

Glad CODEX is running well for you. We draw the plot for ATRX region in our paper using R from scratch. Each black line is a normalized log ratio over the region for one sample. The red regions are where CNVs are detected. I don't have the code any more and even if I do it will not be very generalized at all.

Y is the raw depth of coverage and this should be Y_qc in your code.
lambda is the expected depth of coverage if there is no CNVs. This is Yhat[[optK]] in your code.

You can take the log ratio of these two matrices and it will return a matrix (exons x samples or vice versa). You can then zoon into a region and plot for each sample. start(ref_qc) and end(ref_qc) give you the starting and ending positions for your exonic targets after QC.

I hope this is of help to you. Alternatively, you can load your results in IGV for direct visualization without the need for coding the script yourself. Refer to the section "Visualization by IGV" in our GitHub page here. https://github.com/yuchaojiang/CODEX 


Cheers,
Yuchao
